title: Model tier defaults
description: Contract for law/policy/model-tiers.json, the repository default of the campaign models block under ADR-MDL-0002. The document declares the hosts a campaign may run on, each with the runtime bridge from law/policy/model-runtime-registry.json it resolves through and the model aliases that host publishes; the tiers with their rank, one alias per declared host keyed by host id, a default effort, and a use_for text; the Article 19 escalation rule; and a policy_version. A campaign overrides the default by tier name only and never introduces a host. The resolved map is pinned on each task at task_start together with policy_version, so a later change to this document never reinterprets a started task. The default is law and changes only through a law commit that bumps policy_version.

policy_version.description: Bumped by every change to a host, an alias, a tier, or the escalation rule. Pinned on each task at task_start.

description.description: Human text; it documents, among other things, the collision between the tier named architect and the discipline named architect.

hosts.description: Every host a campaign task may run on, keyed by host id. A campaign cannot introduce a host; host admission is a registry and credential decision.

tiers.description: The tiers, keyed by tier name. Tier names are the only model names prompts and tasks use.

ceiling.description: Tier name past which no escalation happens. Must be a declared tier.

id_form.description: The registry id form of a resolved entry: the runtime id from law/policy/model-runtime-registry.json, a colon, and the host alias, for example claude-cli:fable.

model_alias.description: A model alias the host publishes, as the host CLI accepts it.

effort.description: The tier effort grammar. An effort outside it fails closed.

runtime.description: The id of the runtime bridge in law/policy/model-runtime-registry.json this host resolves through. It must exist there and its family must match the host.

aliases.description: The aliases this host publishes. Every tier entry for the host names one of them.

rank.description: 1 is the highest capability. Escalation moves to a lower rank number. Ranks are unique across tiers.

hosts.description: One alias per declared host, keyed by host id. Every declared host appears, and every alias is one the host declares.

examples.description: Example default with one host and two tiers.

escalation.trigger: one failed iteration or a blocked task

resolution.override: a campaign overrides by tier name; a tier it does not name resolves to this default
